title: Etale source locality of the canonical relative adjunction line
statement:
Let $S$ be a Noetherian scheme (locally Noetherian [pqf-def-locnoeth] and quasi-compact [def-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-scheme]). Let $f:T\to S$ be flat [def-weil-flat-morphism] and finitely presented, meaning locally of finite presentation [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation], quasi-compact [def-weil-finite-type-morphism] and quasi-separated [def-weil-quasi-separated-morphism], with every nonempty geometric fibre pure of dimension one [def-weil-geometric-fibre, def-kun-topological-krull-dimension]. Assume $f$ has regular local complete-intersection presentations as in [lem-trf-flat-lci-canonical-adjunction]: locally it factors through a closed immersion into an open of $\mathbf A^n_S$ with ideal generated by a regular sequence of length $n-1$ [def-weil-pbc-regular-sequence]. Let $e:V\to T$ be an etale finitely presented morphism [def-weil-etale-morphism]. Then $fe:V\to S$ has the same flat, finite-presentation, pure-dimensional and local complete-intersection properties, and the adjunction lines of [lem-trf-flat-lci-canonical-adjunction] admit a canonical isomorphism
$$e^*K_{T/S}\xrightarrow{\sim}K_{V/S}$$
[def-pc-module-pullback, def-sc-invertible-module]. It commutes with restriction to open subschemes and with composition of etale source morphisms. On the inverse image of the relative smooth locus of $T/S$ [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms], it identifies, under the canonical smooth-locus identifications of the adjunction lines, with the usual differential pullback isomorphism $e^*\Omega^1_{T/S}\xrightarrow{\sim}\Omega^1_{V/S}$ [def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials]. No properness, nodal hypothesis, marking, modification morphism, or normality is assumed.

source.place: Tags 0B6V (lemma-lci-shriek), 0FWI (lemma-shriek-etale), with composition of upper shriek, and the smooth-locus conormal identification in Tag 0E9Z (lemma-fundamental-class-lci). Agent-formulated canonical adjunction-line specialization; these tags supply its coherent-duality route.

proof.text: First check finiteness and flatness. Etaleness includes flatness, so composition of flat local-ring maps gives flatness of $fe$ by [lem-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map-comp]. Local finite presentation of $fe$ follows from [lem-sbc-locally-finite-presentation-composition]. For an affine open $A\subset S$, $f^{-1}(A)$ is quasi-compact, and [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-morphism-preimage-qc-open] applied to $e$ makes $e^{-1}f^{-1}(A)$ quasi-compact. Thus $fe$ is quasi-compact. Since $f$ and $e$ are of finite type, [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian] makes first $T$, then $V$, Noetherian. Hence $V$ is quasi-separated by [lem-weil-pbc-locally-noetherian-quasi-separated], and [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence](1) implies that $V\to S$ is quasi-separated. Thus $fe$ is finitely presented in precisely the three-part sense of the statement.

source.place: Tags 00HC (algebra.tex, lemma-composition-flat), 01TR (morphisms.tex, lemma-composition-finite-presentation), 01K4 (schemes.tex, lemma-quasi-compact-affine), 01T6 and 01OY; no separatedness assumption is introduced.

proof.text: Fix a point of $V$ and a presentation of $T/S$ near its image. After taking a principal affine piece of the ambient open, write $A=R[x_1,\ldots,x_n]_q$ and $B=A/(f_1,\ldots,f_{n-1})$, with the displayed regular sequence. By [lem-weil-pbc-etale-locally-standard], a neighbourhood of the chosen point over $\operatorname{Spec}B$ has algebra $C=B[t]_h/(g)$ with $g$ monic. Lift $g$ to a monic $G\in A[t]$ and $h$ to $H\in A[t]$. Then $C=A[t]_H/(f_1,\ldots,f_{n-1},G)$. Multiplication by each $f_i$ remains injective in the successive polynomial quotients, by comparing coefficients. After the $f_i$, multiplication by $G$ is injective because its leading coefficient is $1$: the leading coefficient of a nonzero polynomial cannot vanish in the product. The weak regularity conditions survive localization at $H$ by [lem-exc-weakly-regular-sequence-localization]. At points of $\operatorname{Spec}C$ the final quotient is nonzero, so these are regular local equations by [def-weil-pbc-regular-sequence]. The ambient scheme is open in $\mathbf A^{n+1}_S$, with exactly $n=(n+1)-1$ equations. This proves the required local presentation property of $fe$.

source.place: Tag 00UE (algebra.tex, proposition-etale-locally-standard); regularity verified coefficientwise, then localized as in Tag 07P9 (more-algebra.tex, lemma-intersection-regular-with-closed).

proof.text: For a geometric point $\bar s\to S$, the source map $e_{\bar s}:V_{\bar s}\to T_{\bar s}$ is etale by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-scheme-base-change]. Finite-presentation base change in [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence](3) makes both fibres locally of finite type over the geometric residue field. These fibres are locally Noetherian by [pqf-lem-locnoeth-lft], since they are locally of finite type over the geometric residue field. If $V_{\bar s}$ is nonempty, so is $T_{\bar s}$; its pure dimension one gives $\dim_tT_{\bar s}=1$ at every point by [lem-sbc-equidimensional-open-local-dimension], applied with the whole fibre as open. By [lem-weil-pbc-etale-smooth-zero-dimensional-fibres], $e_{\bar s}$ is smooth of relative dimension zero. The local topological dimension formula [lem-per-smooth-local-dimension] therefore gives $\dim_vV_{\bar s}=1+0=1$ for every $v$. Now [lem-sbc-constant-local-dimension-components] with the whole fibre as open shows every irreducible component has dimension one. Empty fibres require no assertion.

By [lem-weil-pbc-regular-sequence-koszul-regular], the regular local equations for both morphisms are Koszul-regular. Put $L_T=L_{T/S}$ and $L_V=L_{V/S}$. Their local conormal models $E_i=[I/I^2\to i^*\Omega^1_{P/S}]$ and comparisons $\lambda_i:E_i\simeq L|_U$ from [lem-trf-lci-cotangent-presentation] are perfect of amplitude $[-1,0]$, so [lem-trf-two-term-perfect-determinant] applies to $L_T$ and $L_V$. Steps 1--3 show that $V/S$ satisfies the hypotheses of [lem-trf-flat-lci-canonical-adjunction] with $d=1$, as $T/S$ does. Apply [lem-sfb-adjunction-cotangent-determinant-normalization] to $T/S$ and to $V/S$: it gives canonical isomorphisms $\theta_T:K_{T/S}\simeq\det L_T$ and $\theta_V:K_{V/S}\simeq\det L_V$ such that, on every presentation chart, $K_i\to K|_U\xrightarrow{\theta}\det L|_U$ is the exterior-model identification $K_i=D(E_i)$ followed by $\det(\lambda_i)$; in particular the specified adjunction transitions are $\det(\lambda_j^{-1}\lambda_i)$. So both lines are compared with determinants through the specified presentation comparisons, not through independently chosen isomorphisms. On a smooth chart the canonical augmentation of [lem-trf-lci-cotangent-presentation] is an isomorphism $L\simeq\Omega^1[0]$, and $\det(\Omega^1[0])=\Omega^1$ since the relative dimension is one. The composite of $\theta$ with the determinant of this augmentation is the canonical comparison of [lem-trf-two-term-perfect-determinant] between the models $E_i$ and $\Omega^1[0]$, i.e. the smooth-locus identification $K\cong\Omega^1$ of [lem-trf-flat-lci-canonical-adjunction]. These identifications fix the normalization used below.

source.place: Tags 08SL (proposition-cotangent-complex-local-complete-intersection), 0FJX and 0FJY (perfect.tex); the same conormal determinant as the proof of duality.tex Tag 0E9Z.

proof.text: Since $e$ is locally of finite presentation, choose affine charts on which the ring maps of $e$ are finitely presented, as in [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation]. These ring maps are formally etale by the unique infinitesimal lifting assertion of [lem-weil-pbc-flat-unramified-formally-etale]. Consequently [lem-trf-etale-cotangent-vanishing] makes their full cotangent complexes zero. The affine comparison of [lem-trf-lci-cotangent-presentation] identifies these with restrictions of $L_{V/T}$. Hence $L_{V/T}=0$: all its cohomology sheaves vanish on an affine cover. The triangle of [lem-sfb-scheme-cotangent-transitivity], applied to $V\xrightarrow{e}T\xrightarrow{f}S$, now gives an isomorphism $u_e:Le^*L_T\xrightarrow{\sim}L_V$. Indeed the third term is zero, so the long exact cohomology sequence makes the first arrow a quasi-isomorphism. This is the specified functoriality arrow, not a choice of an isomorphism between the two objects.

Define the required line map by the composite
$$\Phi_e:e^*K_{T/S}\xrightarrow{e^*\theta_T}e^*\det L_T\xrightarrow{\rho_e}\det(Le^*L_T)\xrightarrow{\det(u_e)}\det L_V\xrightarrow{\theta_V^{-1}}K_{V/S},$$
where $\theta_T,\theta_V$ are the normalized comparisons of [lem-sfb-adjunction-cotangent-determinant-normalization] from step 4 and $\rho_e$ is the natural pullback comparison of [lem-trf-two-term-perfect-determinant]. All arrows are isomorphisms. Since $\theta$ is fixed by the presentation comparisons, this is an isomorphism of the specified adjunction lines, independent of the chosen chart or standard-etale presentation.

source.place: perfect.tex, Tag 0FJY (remark-functorial-det), applied to the canonical cotangent arrow of the preceding step.

proof.text:
For a further etale finitely presented $a:W\to V$, [lem-sfb-scheme-cotangent-transitivity] gives $u_{e\circ a}=u_a\circ La^*u_e$ after the canonical pullback association. Write $\rho_a(F):a^*\det F\to\det(La^*F)$. The naturality clause of [lem-trf-two-term-perfect-determinant] gives
$$\det(La^*u_e)\rho_a(Le^*L_T)=\rho_a(L_V)a^*\det(u_e).$$
Its composition clause gives $\rho_{e\circ a}(L_T)=\rho_a(Le^*L_T)a^*\rho_e(L_T)$. Substitute both identities into the formula of step 6, where the middle factors $a^*\theta_V$ and $a^*\theta_V^{-1}$ cancel and $(e\circ a)^*\theta_T=a^*e^*\theta_T$, and use $\det(u_a\circ La^*u_e)=\det(u_a)\det(La^*u_e)$ to obtain
$$\Phi_{e\circ a}=\Phi_a\circ a^*\Phi_e.$$
Identity arrows give the identity since $u_1=1$, $\det(1)=1$ and $\rho_1=1$.

source.place: Tag 08QL (section-functoriality), and perfect.tex Tags 0FJX, 0FJY; substitution of the stated naturality and composition laws.

proof.text: For open restrictions of $T$ or $V$, restrict the intrinsic complexes and the arrow $u_e$. The restriction clause of [lem-sfb-scheme-cotangent-transitivity] gives exactly the cotangent arrow of the restricted morphism. The restriction and naturality clauses of [lem-trf-two-term-perfect-determinant] identify its determinant and $\rho$ with the restrictions of the original ones. Thus the formula for $\Phi_e$ restricts to the same formula on these opens. In particular open source restrictions compose as in the preceding step. This uses arbitrary affine covers and checks equality of sheaf maps locally; it does not require affine intersections or separatedness.

source.place: Tags 08T3, 08QL, and perfect.tex Tags 0FJX, 0FJY; restriction of the defining composite.

proof.text: Let $U\subset T$ be the relative smooth locus and $V_U=e^{-1}U$. The restriction $U\to S$ is smooth of relative dimension one; etale $V_U\to U$ is smooth of relative dimension zero. By [lem-sbc-smooth-relative-dimension-permanence] the composite $V_U\to S$ is smooth of relative dimension one. By [lem-trf-lci-cotangent-presentation], the canonical augmentations on these opens identify $L_T|_U$ and $L_V|_{V_U}$ with their differential sheaves in degree zero. The augmentation clause of [lem-sfb-scheme-cotangent-transitivity] identifies $u_e$ in this diagram with the usual map $e^*\Omega^1_{U/S}\to\Omega^1_{V_U/S}$, locally $r\otimes\mathrm db\mapsto r\,\mathrm d(e^\sharp b)$. Thus it is an isomorphism. By [lem-sc-smooth-omega-finite-locally-free], both differential sheaves are locally free of rank one. Determinant of a rank-one module in degree zero is that module, and determinant of its map is the map itself. Apply [lem-trf-two-term-perfect-determinant], the normalization $\theta$ of [lem-sfb-adjunction-cotangent-determinant-normalization] and the smooth identifications of [lem-trf-flat-lci-canonical-adjunction] from step 4 to the defining composite: $\Phi_e|_{V_U}$ is exactly this differential pullback map. This proves the stated normalization, with no density assumption on the smooth locus.
